Upstream fixes:
- https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/017e3f89b081e4828a588a3bd27b5feacea042b7
- https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/35c98149a5c7af9159fa7615d8d827b3aaa3cc97
- https://github.com/gcc-mirror/gcc/commit/8b3e47b4099f319e38d357f7c646f51040a13d6e

Suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36271#issuecomment-5794127014.

[2026-10-23] c:6365775124 comment by hebasto (member):
I have to admit that I can’t see a real-life scenario in which the bug affects users.

The code is reachable only when migrating a legacy BDB wallet, either via the `migratewallet` RPC command or via the GUI.

The `dest` argument of `BerkeleyRODatabase::Backup()` is constructed in `MigrateLegacyToDescriptor()` and includes a timestamp. If a migration attempt fails for any reason, the next attempt is very likely to write a differently named file. However, the bug can only be hit if the backup file has the same name.
[2026-10-23] c:6371922580 comment by theuni (member):
It seems to me this is either:
- A compiler config not worth worrying about
- A compiler config worth explicitly blocking as suggested by @maflcko
- A compiler config we're worried about, in which case we could just remove the `copy_options` param from `copy_file` so that we can't hit this anywhere else.

Either way, adding a test that fails where we expect it to fail doesn't seem very helpful to me.
